resolutions.finding: C1: R048 documents RowDrag.settle with pastCentre and a Bool-returning move closure that gates the loop; R025 records settle(order:heights:fallbackHeight:swap:) with a Void closure.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/RowDrag.swift:30-36 declares `mutating func settle(order: [ID], heights: [ID: CGFloat], fallbackHeight: CGFloat, pastCentre: CGFloat = 0, move: (_ neighbour: ID, _ placeAfter: Bool) -> Bool) -> Bool`. There is no `swap:` label anywhere in the file. The crossing loop at RowDrag.swift:41-58 gates on the closure's return: line 46 `guard offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre, move(next, true) else { break }` and line 52 `guard -offset > (own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre, move(previous, false) else { break }`. Only after a true return does it do `settled += slot` / `settled -= slot`, advance `current` and set `moved = true`. `visualOffset` is `translation - settled` (RowDrag.swift:15). Call site DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift:783-794: `let moved = drag.settle(order: order, heights: snapshot.heights, fallbackHeight: Chrome.rowHeight + 1) { neighbour, placeAfter in withAnimation(Self.slide) { if let group { model.moveInActivity(id, to: neighbour, placeAfter: placeAfter, among: group) } else { model.moveThread(id, to: neighbour, placeAfter: placeAfter) } } }` - the trailing closure's value is the Bool that `withAnimation` forwards from the model call. AppModel.swift:338 `@discardableResult func moveThread(_ id: UUID, to targetID: UUID, placeAfter: Bool) -> Bool` and AppModel.swift:358 `@discardableResult func moveInActivity(_ id: UUID, to targetID: UUID, placeAfter: Bool, among peers: [UUID]) -> Bool`. moveThread returns false when id == targetID, either thread is missing, projects differ, the project is missing, either thread isSettled, the target is not in the order, or `order != before` fails (AppModel.swift:339-347). RowDrag.swift:22-28 states in a comment why the compensation must live in settle and not in move: settle is a mutating call on a copy of the caller's @State, so writes to the state from inside move are clobbered.
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows reorder helper must take a 4th optional parameter pastCentre defaulting to 0, and its move callback must return bool. The crossing loop must break on a false return WITHOUT advancing the index or adjusting the settled compensation, and must return whether anything moved. A void callback makes a refused move loop forever (the offset condition stays satisfied, the row never advances, and in the source the guard is what stops it). The offset test is strictly `>` and includes the `slot * pastCentre` term. The caller must feed `fallbackHeight = rowHeight + 1` (28 + 1 = 29) and must recompute the peer snapshot and fire an alignment haptic only when settle returned true (SidebarView.swift:795-800).

resolutions.finding: C2: R024 says the FloatingSidebarPanel resize is clamped with the minimum size as the lower bound.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. DroppyCode/App/Views/Sidebar/FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:74-77 (resize path): `var next = CGSize(width: start.width + translation.width, height: start.height + translation.height)` ; `next.width = min(max(Self.minSize.width, next.width), area.width - origin.x - Self.margin)` ; `next.height = min(max(Self.minSize.height, next.height), area.height - origin.y - Self.margin)` ; `model.settings.sidebarPanelSize = next`. The outer `min` is applied last, so when `area.width - origin.x - 12 < 240` the written width is below minSize.width, and likewise for height when `area.height - origin.y - 12 < 320`. minSize is `CGSize(width: 240, height: 320)` (line 18), margin is 12 (line 19), defaultSize is `CGSize(width: 300, height: 560)` (line 17), stripHeight 44 (line 20). The value is written to settings on that same drag tick (line 77), i.e. persisted immediately, not at drag end. The READ path at lines 29-32 is different arithmetic and does keep minSize as a floor on both arms: `width: min(max(Self.minSize.width, stored.width), max(Self.minSize.width, area.width - Self.margin * 2))`, `height: min(max(Self.minSize.height, stored.height), max(Self.minSize.height, area.height - Self.margin * 2))`. So a sub-minimum size can be persisted but is floored again when read back.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce both arithmetics exactly and do not unify them. Write path: min(max(240, w), areaW - originX - 12) and min(max(320, h), areaH - originY - 12), persisted on every drag tick. Read path: min(max(240, storedW), max(240, areaW - 24)) and min(max(320, storedH), max(320, areaH - 24)). The port must accept that a sub-240 or sub-320 value can reach the settings store.

resolutions.finding: G1: the resize path can persist a sidebarPanelSize smaller than minSize; and the resize clamp is anchored on origin = dragOrigin ?? rest.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. FloatingSidebarPanel.swift:33-34 computes `let rest = Self.clamp(model.settings.sidebarPanelOrigin ?? CGPoint(x: Self.margin, y: Chrome.contentTopInset), size: size, in: area)` then `let origin = dragOrigin ?? rest`. That same `origin` is captured by the resize closure at lines 75-76, so while the strip is held (dragOrigin non-nil) a simultaneous resize clamps against the dragged origin. The default resting origin is therefore literally CGPoint(x: 12, y: 72), because Chrome.contentTopInset = chromeTopPadding + capsuleHeight + contentBreathBelowChrome = 12 + 32 + 28 = 72 (Chrome.swift:32, 33, 34, 38, 39, 40). The static clamp (lines 121-126) is `x: min(max(margin, origin.x), max(margin, area.width - size.width - margin))`, `y: min(max(margin, origin.y), max(margin, area.height - size.height - margin))` - this one DOES keep margin as a floor on both arms, unlike the resize clamp. resizeStart is latched on the first tick (`let start = resizeStart ?? size; resizeStart = start`, lines 72-73) and cleared in onDragEnd (line 79). Origin is persisted only at drag end (line 116 `if let dragOrigin { model.settings.sidebarPanelOrigin = dragOrigin }`), while size is persisted on every tick (line 77). The panel's slide animation is `.animation(dragOrigin == nil ? Chrome.panelSlide : nil, value: origin)` (line 104) - no animation while dragging.
resolutions.port_impact: Default resting origin is the literal (12, 72). Resize clamps against the live origin (dragged if mid-drag), size persists per tick, origin persists on release only, and no animation is applied to origin while the strip is held.

resolutions.finding: G13: AppModel.settledFirst's updatedAt fallback left unresolved.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. AppModel.swift:377-380: `/// The order among settled threads: the one settled last comes first.` then `nonisolated static func settledFirst(_ lhs: ChatThread, _ rhs: ChatThread) -> Bool { (lhs.settledAt ?? lhs.updatedAt) > (rhs.settledAt ?? rhs.updatedAt) }`. Strict `>`, so equal keys are not reordered by this predicate and the sort's own stability decides. The fallback to updatedAt is exactly what orders threads settled before settledAt was persisted. resolutions.finding: G15: KeyChord.allowedModifiers left unresolved though it gates two shipped key paths.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT on the value, PARTLY WRONG on one attribution. Shortcuts.swift:6 `static let allowedModifiers: NSEvent.ModifierFlags = [.control, .option, .shift, .command]` - exactly 4 elements: control, option, shift, command. Fn, capsLock, function, numericPad, help and the device-independent mask bits are all excluded. It is applied in KeyChord.init (Shortcuts.swift:13 `self.modifiers = modifiers.intersection(Self.allowedModifiers).rawValue`) and in modifierFlags (Shortcuts.swift:17). Gated shipped paths: (a) SidebarView.swift:948-955, the archive popover's local keyDown monitor: `guard event.window is ThreadWindow, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers).isEmpty else { return event }` then `case 36, 76: onArchive() // Return, keypad Enter` and `case 53: onDismiss() // Escape`. (b) ThreadWindow.swift:11-17, the Cmd-digit monitor: `guard let self, event.window === self, attachedSheet == nil, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers) == .command, let number = Self.digitKeyCodes[event.keyCode], let selectThreadNumber else { return event }`, with ThreadWindow.swift:23 `private static let digitKeyCodes: [UInt16: Int] = [18: 1, 19: 2, 20: 3, 21: 4, 23: 5, 22: 6, 26: 7, 28: 8, 25: 9]` (9 entries; 23 maps to 5 and 22 maps to 6, which is the real macOS key-code order). CRITIC WRONG ON ONE POINT: the Escape close at ThreadWindow.swift:48-56 belongs to `SecondaryWindow` (declared ThreadWindow.swift:44), not to ThreadWindow: `override func sendEvent(_ event: NSEvent) { if event.type == .keyDown, event.keyCode == 53, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers).isEmpty, !(firstResponder is NSText) { performClose(nil); return }; super.sendEvent(event) }`, plus a Cmd-W equivalent at ThreadWindow.swift:58-60 `if attachedSheet == nil, KeyChord(keyCode: Int(event.keyCode), modifiers: event.modifierFlags) == KeyChord(keyCode: 13, modifiers: .command) { performClose(nil) }`. ThreadWindow's own extra key handling is performKeyEquivalent for keyCode 48 (Tab) at ThreadWindow.swift:25-38, matched against ShortcutStore chords for .nextThread / .previousThread.
resolutions.port_impact: Mask every observed modifier state to {Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win} before comparing or persisting a chord; ignore CapsLock, NumLock, Scroll and the extended/numpad flag. Popover Return / keypad-Enter / Escape must require an empty masked modifier set. Cmd-digit becomes the port's single-modifier-digit chord with the masked set exactly equal to that one modifier, over key codes 1..9 in that order. Escape-to-close and the close chord belong to the secondary window class, and Escape is skipped while a text field has focus.

resolutions.finding: G18: the same RowAction runs with different timing in PopoverItem vs RowActionMenuButtons; the sidebar's two Settle paths differ.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT: the asymmetry is real, but there are THREE timings, not two, and the cited line numbers are off. Popovers.swift:257-274, PopoverItem's Button action: (1) confirmation branch, lines 259-269: when `confirmation != nil, !isConfirmed` it calls `action()` SYNCHRONOUSLY at line 262, then `withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.22)) { isConfirmed = true }` (line 263), then defers only the close into `Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(for: Self.confirmationHold); if let close = closePopoverBox?.close { close() } else { dismiss() } }` (lines 264-267) and returns. (2) `guard !isConfirmed else { return }` (line 270) swallows a second press on an already-confirmed row. (3) plain branch, lines 271-273: close first (`if let close = closePopoverBox?.close { close() } else { dismiss() }`), then `// Runs after the popover closes, so an action that presents a sheet or alert is not swallowed.` and `Task { @MainActor in action() }`. Popovers.swift:365-382, RowActionMenuButtons: `ForEach(actions) { item in if item.startsGroup { Divider() }; Button(role: item.isDestructive ? .destructive : nil) { item.action() } label: { if let symbol = item.symbol { Label(item.title, systemImage: symbol) } else { Text(item.title) } } }` - `item.action()` at Popovers.swift:372, called synchronously in the menu callback. The two sidebar Settle actions are genuinely different code built by two different factories: ThreadActions.make (SidebarView.swift:2194 onward, the ellipsis popover) builds the settle RowAction at SidebarView.swift:2229-2242 whose body is `if thread.isSettled { if let onReopen { onReopen() } else { model.reopenAnimated(thread.id) } } else if let onSettle { onSettle() } else { model.settleAnimated(thread.id) }` - it calls the row's own handlers. ThreadActions.makeContextMenu (SidebarView.swift:2257 onward, the AppKit context menu) builds it at SidebarView.swift:2298-2306 whose body is `[weak model, threadID, isSettled] in guard let model else { return }; model.finishRequest = AppModel.FinishRequest(threadID: threadID, reopens: isSettled)`. The doc comment at SidebarView.swift:2249-2253 states why: the AppKit menu outlives the right-click, so its callbacks must not retain the row or its settle handlers; settle and reopen post a finish request which the row takes up (SidebarView.swift:1866-1870 `.onChange(of: model.finishRequest) { _, request in guard let request, request.threadID == thread.id, request.reopens == isSettled else { return }; model.finishRequest = nil; if request.reopens { reopen() } else { settle() } }`), and AppModel.finishSelectedThread (AppModel.swift:856-871) has an 80 ms `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(80))` no-taker fallback. Titles in both factories are identical: 'Reopen' / 'Settle' with symbols 'arrow.uturn.backward' / 'checkmark.circle', and 'Archive' with 'archivebox', ordered `settleFirst ? [settle, archive] : [archive, settle]`, with 'Delete...' / 'trash' destructive last and 'Reveal worktree in Finder' / 'folder' when a worktree path exists.
resolutions.port_impact: Three call timings to reproduce: confirmation rows act immediately and close after the hold; plain popover rows close first and act on the next main-loop turn (so a sheet-presenting action survives); context-menu rows act synchronously. The context menu must never capture the row - it posts a finish request with an 80 ms no-taker fallback, while the popover calls the row's own settle/reopen so the ghost flies. Both paths use the same strings and the same settleFirst ordering.

resolutions.finding: G19: HeadCardsRow adds a chevron row to cardRows when capped, while the slotHeights drag fallback does not.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT: correct, and there is a SECOND divergence the critic did not name. SidebarView.swift:1443-1444: `let capped = heads.count > 12` ; `let visible = showsAllHeads ? heads : Array(heads.prefix(12))`. SidebarView.swift:1462-1463: `let rows = Self.chunk(visible, by: perRow)` ; `let cardRows = rows.count + (capped ? 1 : 0)`, and cardRows feeds `ThreadRowMetrics.headCardHeight(rows: cardRows)` at SidebarView.swift:1468-1469. The extra row exists because of the chevron button at SidebarView.swift:1515-1520 (`if capped { Button { withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.18)) { showsAllHeads.toggle() } } label: { Image(systemName: showsAllHeads ? "chevron.up" : "chevron.down").font(.system(size: 9, weight: .semibold)) ... } }`). The drag-slot fallback, SidebarView.swift:846-848: `if headCount > 0 { let rows = (headCount + 5) / 6; height += (rowHeights.values["heads-<id>"] ?? ThreadRowMetrics.headCardHeight(rows: rows)) + 1 }`. It (a) never adds the capped chevron row and (b) assumes SIX glyphs per row, while HeadCardsRow uses seven until the card is measured and a width-derived count afterwards (SidebarView.swift:1453 `let perRow = width == 0 ? 7 : max(1, Int((usable + ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphPitch - ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphSize) / ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphPitch))`). Metrics: headGlyphSize 14 (:1296), headBadgeOverhang 3 (:1302), headRowGap 6 (:1304), headCardPadding 6 (:1305), connectorWidth 28 (:1292), helperHeight 24 (:1278). ThreadRowMetrics.headCardHeight (SidebarView.swift:1309-1312): `let rows = max(1, rows); return 2 * headCardPadding + CGFloat(rows) * headGlyphSize + CGFloat(rows - 1) * headRowGap` = 12 + rows*14 + (rows-1)*6. Row gap distribution, SidebarView.swift:1458-1461: `let tightGap = ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphPitch - ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphSize` then `let rowGap = perRow > 1 && width > 0 ? max(tightGap, (usable - CGFloat(perRow) * ThreadRowMetrics.headGlyphSize) / CGFloat(perRow - 1)) : tightGap`. Card key for the measured height is the literal string 'heads-<id>'; the helper-block key is 'helpers-<id>' (SidebarView.swift:838). Each measured or fallback block adds a trailing + 1.

resolutions.finding: G20: RowFrames.thread(at:) picks from a Dictionary in unspecified hash order when frames overlap.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with corrected lines. SidebarView.swift:2457-2473: `private final class RowFrames { private var frames: [UUID: CGRect] = [:]; func note(_ id: UUID, _ frame: CGRect) { guard frames[id] != frame else { return }; frames[id] = frame }; func forget(_ id: UUID) { frames[id] = nil }; func thread(at point: CGPoint) -> UUID? { frames.first { $0.value.contains(point) }?.key } }`. `thread(at:)` is at SidebarView.swift:2470-2472 (the critic's 2465-2467 is off by five). `Dictionary.first(where:)` iterates in the dictionary's own storage order, which for UUID keys under Swift's per-process hash seed is neither insertion order nor z-order and is not stable between runs. The class doc (SidebarView.swift:2455-2456) says the frames are kept out of observation and only the grab of a drag reads them.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE-LEVEL NON-DETERMINISM. An ordered list or a z-order-aware hit test would behave differently when two row frames overlap (mid-animation or during a settle handover). Record it as an upstream defect; a hash-map-backed implementation reproduces it, an ordered one does not. Do not 'fix' it by taking the topmost row.

resolutions.finding: G21: makeCaptureWindow uses the default windowClass, not ThreadWindow.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. WindowManager.swift:74-78: `/// The main window for the website captures: the same window, at a fixed size, with` / `/// no frame autosave, so the run never reads or writes where the real window sits.` / `func makeCaptureWindow(size: NSSize) -> NSWindow { makeWindow(title: AppInfo.name, size: size, resizable: true) { RootView() } }` - no windowClass argument. So the capture window carries NO Cmd-1..9 digit monitor (ThreadWindow.swift:8-19 installs it from selectThreadNumber's didSet, which makeCaptureWindow never sets) and NO Tab next/previous-thread chords (ThreadWindow.swift:25-38). resolutions.finding: X4 (cross-cutting): Reduce Motion is a global kill switch read in nine places.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, every site verified. (1) Chrome.swift:98-102 `static var panelSlide: Animation { NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.18) : .spring(response: 0.32, dampingFraction: 0.9) }`. (2) Chrome.swift:110-114 `static var settleFlight: Animation { ... ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(glideSpring) }` with glideSpring `Spring(response: 0.6, dampingRatio: 0.86)` (Chrome.swift:106). (3) WindowChrome.swift:280 `private static var slideRun: Int { NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion ? 220 : 420 }`, awaited as `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(Self.slideRun))` at WindowChrome.swift:315. (4) WindowChrome.swift:223-228 `let reduceMotion = NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion; NSAnimationContext.runAnimationGroup { context in context.duration = reduceMotion ? 0.18 : 0.32; context.timingFunction = CAMediaTimingFunction(name: .easeOut); context.allowsImplicitAnimation = true; titlebar.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded() }`, preceded by `guard animated, !window.inLiveResize else { titlebar.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded(); return }` (WindowChrome.swift:216-220). (5) RowGlide.swift:76 `guard from.width > 1, from.height > 1, !NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion else { return }` in RowGlideAnimator.launch. (6) Genie.swift:63-64 `guard from.width > 1, from.height > 1, to.width > 1, to.height > 1, !NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion else { return false }` in morph. (7) Genie.swift:83-84 the same guard in launch, returning false. (8) HydraGlyph.swift:192 `guard !NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion else { return }` before installing the CABasicAnimation on 'transform.scale' from restingScale to swollenScale in HydraBreathRing (declared HydraGlyph.swift:72-74). (9) Chrome.swift:943-948 SettleGlideModifier, where reduce motion gives `fade = progress` (linear), `.offset(y: 0)` and `.scaleEffect(1)`. The spinners use the SwiftUI environment key instead of the workspace flag: WorkingIndicators.swift:78 `SpinnerCells(cells: Self.cells, columns: 3, cellSize: cellSize, animated: !reduceMotion, theme: ThemeManager.current)` with `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion` (also at WorkingIndicators.swift:89 for MiniSpinner).
resolutions.port_impact: Read SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION at each query point (the source reads the live flag every time, not a cached value) and apply it at all nine sites with the exact substitutes: 180 ms ease-out for the panel slide, 200 ms ease-out for the settle flight, a 220 ms slide run instead of 420, 180 ms instead of 320 for caption-button placement, refuse the row glide entirely, return false from both genie entry points so the caller shows the real thing, install no breath ring animation, freeze the spinner cells at their per-cell phase, and fade the settle badge in place with no offset and no scale.

resolutions.finding: X5 (cross-cutting): two animations depend on rasterizing a live SwiftUI tree to a bitmap.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. RowGlide.swift:131-137 `func render<Face: View>(_ face: Face, size: CGSize, colorScheme: ColorScheme) -> NSImage? { let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: face.frame(width: size.width, height: size.height, alignment: .topLeading).environment(\.colorScheme, colorScheme)); renderer.scale = NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2; return renderer.nsImage }`. Genie.swift:85-88 `let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: GenieGhost(size: frame.size, content: ghost()).environment(\.colorScheme, colorScheme)); renderer.scale = NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2; guard let image = renderer.nsImage else { return false }`. Both use the same fallback scale literal 2. The two-face discipline is real: SidebarView.swift:1938-1948 builds an `arriving` copy of the thread with `arriving.isSettled = settled` and, when settling, `arriving.isPinned = false; arriving.hasUnread = false`, then picks `let arrivalHeight = settled ? ThreadRowMetrics.settledHeight : (projectName != nil ? ThreadRowMetrics.detailedHeight : Chrome.rowHeight)`; the row's own trailing clearance (SidebarView.swift:1896-1899) is `if showsActions { return (isSettled ? 30 : 52) + (showsFold ? 20 : 0) }; return isDetailed || isSettled ? 18 : 52`. The still-spinner exists solely for this: WorkingIndicators.swift:86-88 `/// Draws one still frame with plain shapes instead of hosting a layer view. For image` / `/// renderers, which cannot capture AppKit views: the archive ghost is rendered this way.` / `var isStill = false`, branched at WorkingIndicators.swift:104 `if isStill {`, with its single call site SidebarView.swift:2101 `MiniSpinner(cellSize: 2.4, isStill: true)`. The genie flight is launched from the row at SidebarView.swift:1996 `GenieAnimator.shared.launch(frame: windowFrame.frame, colorScheme: colorScheme) { ... }`. RowGlideAnimator also carries a landing window: `land(threadID:settled:at:)` only accepts a landing while `Date.now.timeIntervalSince(glides[index].launchedAt) < Self.landingWindow` and the direction matches (RowGlide.swift:86-90).
resolutions.port_impact: The port needs a view-to-bitmap capture at the display scale factor (fallback 2), a second 'arriving' face rendered with different trailing clearance and a different row height, and a shapes-only still spinner variant for the captured face. Without all three the settle, reopen and archive animations cannot be reproduced.

resolutions.finding: X6 (cross-cutting): DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow and DCNotificationGuard are macOS-only AppKit exception nets.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. They are Objective-C, not Swift: DroppyCode/App/Window/DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow.h:33 `@interface DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow : NSWindow`, implemented in DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow.m:15, and DroppyCode/App/Window/DCNotificationGuard.m; both are exposed through DroppyCode/App/Window/DroppyCode-Bridging-Header.h:1. Every NSWindow in the app derives from the guarded base: ThreadWindow.swift:3 `final class ThreadWindow: DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow`, ThreadWindow.swift:44 `final class SecondaryWindow: DCDisplayCycleGuardedWindow`, and the default parameter at WindowManager.swift:90. WindowManager.swift:6 states the reason in the source's own words: every window is a guarded window because SwiftUI under a transparent title bar makes AppKit misbehave.
resolutions.port_impact: Do NOT re-implement. Record that the class hierarchy exists only as an AppKit exception net. The portable parts are ThreadWindow's Cmd-digit monitor and Tab chords (see G15) and SecondaryWindow's Escape-and-close-chord handling, not the base class.

resolutions.finding: X7 (cross-cutting): no theme defines a text colour; every text, fill and divider derives from the system label colour.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Chrome.swift:75-77: `// Dynamic system colors resolve at draw time, so one wrapped value serves every appearance.` / `static let primaryText = Color(nsColor: .labelColor)` / `static let secondaryText = Color(nsColor: .secondaryLabelColor)`. Chrome.swift:71-73 `static func overlay(_ opacity: Double) -> Color { primaryText.opacity(opacity) }`. ThemeSpec (AppTheme.swift:205-212) has exactly 6 members and none is a text colour: `var scheme: ColorScheme?`, `var accent: Color?`, `var surface: Color`, `var success: Color`, `var warning: Color`, `var danger: Color`. The .system theme's surface is a dynamic NSColor, AppTheme.swift:181-187: `NSColor(name: nil, dynamicProvider: { appearance in let isDark = appearance.bestMatch(from: [.darkAqua, .aqua]) == .darkAqua; return isDark ? NSColor(srgbRed: 0x1E / 255.0, green: 0x1E / 255.0, blue: 0x20 / 255.0, alpha: 1.0) : NSColor(srgbRed: 1.0, green: 1.0, blue: 1.0, alpha: 1.0) })` - sRGB 1E1E20 dark, FFFFFF light. For every other theme `surfaceColor = Color(hex: palette.surface)` (AppTheme.swift:189). Accent is optional and nil for system/light/dark, falling back to `Color(nsColor: .controlAccentColor)` through Chrome.accent (Chrome.swift:78 and :83) and to `.controlAccentColor` through Chrome.accentNSColor (Chrome.swift:85); success/warning/danger fall back to `.green`/`.orange`/`.red` (AppTheme.swift:194-196).
resolutions.port_impact: Pick the Windows equivalents of labelColor and secondaryLabelColor FIRST (the theme-aware text brushes), because every row fill, card fill, divider and panel scrim in the family is derived from them by opacity. The 26 palettes only supply surface + accent + 3 status hues. System theme surface is literally #1E1E20 dark / #FFFFFF light.

resolutions.finding: X8 (cross-cutting): sidebar launch state and session state are deliberately separate; the sidebar always starts collapsed on a fresh install.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT on the behaviour, WRONG on one mechanical detail. WindowChrome.swift:240-247: `static let minimumWidth: CGFloat = 210`, `static let maximumWidth: CGFloat = 440`, `static let collapseThreshold: CGFloat = 110`, `static let defaultWidth: CGFloat = 268`, `private enum Key { static let width = "sidebarWidth"; static let startsOpen = "sidebarStartsOpen" }`. init (WindowChrome.swift:287-296): `let defaults = CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard; let stored = (defaults.object(forKey: Key.width) as? Double).map { CGFloat($0) } ?? Self.defaultWidth; restingWidth = min(Self.maximumWidth, max(Self.minimumWidth, stored)); width = restingWidth; let visible = defaults.object(forKey: Key.startsOpen) as? Bool ?? false; startsOpen = visible; isVisible = visible; holdsTrafficLights = visible`. So 268 default, clamped 210...440 on read, startsOpen default FALSE, and isVisible and holdsTrafficLights are both seeded from startsOpen alone. CRITIC WRONG ON ONE POINT: persist() DOES touch startsOpen. WindowChrome.swift:366-370: `private func persist() { let defaults = CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard; defaults.set(Double(restingWidth), forKey: Key.width); defaults.set(startsOpen, forKey: Key.startsOpen) }`. It writes BOTH keys, but writes startsOpen's unchanged in-memory value - so the first toggle on a fresh install materialises 'sidebarStartsOpen' = false on disk rather than leaving it absent. The observable behaviour the critic describes is still correct. startsOpen has `didSet { persist() }` (WindowChrome.swift:255-257), which is the Settings toggle's write. endDrag (WindowChrome.swift:344-356): if `width < 110` it calls `beginSlide(delta: width)`, `withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) { isVisible = false }` and restores `width = restingWidth`; otherwise `let settled = max(Self.minimumWidth, width); restingWidth = settled; withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) { width = settled }`; then persist(); then `isDragging = false`. endDrag's floor is minimumWidth only - there is no upper clamp there, because drag(by:) already caps it: WindowChrome.swift:215-217 `func drag(by translation: CGFloat) { width = min(Self.maximumWidth, max(0, anchorWidth + translation)) }` (lower bound 0, not 210). toggle (WindowChrome.swift:358-364): `let opening = !isVisible; if opening { width = restingWidth }; beginSlide(delta: opening ? -restingWidth : width); withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) { isVisible.toggle() }; persist()`. `renderedWidth` is `isVisible ? width : 0` (WindowChrome.swift:298).
resolutions.port_impact: sidebarWidth default 268, clamped 210...440 on read and floored at 210 on drag release; live drag clamps 0...440; collapse threshold 110. sidebarStartsOpen default false and the ONLY thing consulted at launch; the session's open/closed state is never persisted. persist() rewrites both keys on every toggle and every drag release - reproduce that, including the redundant startsOpen write.

In a chat area where `area.width - origin.x - 12 < 240` (or `area.height - origin.y - 12 < 320`) the panel is written SMALLER than minSize (240x320), and line 77 persists that sub-minimum value to settings.sidebarPanelSize on the same drag tick.
